newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps all gain except reluctant naphtha.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps all gain except reluctant naphtha.

text.p: European oil swaps tracked higher on Tuesday with the exception of flat naphtha which looked quiet and resistant to the upwards pull of crude.
Brent CFDs were up to 15 cents stronger, gasoline rose $2, heavy fuel went up nearly $1 and naphtha was unchanged.

Brent CFDs gained about 10 cents for the balance of this week at -47/48 cents against August Brent while next week, June 23-27, gained about 15 cents to -35 cents against August. June 30 to July 5 was pegged at -33 cents and July 7-11 was put at -33/34 cents.
Traders said June 23-27 traded at -36 cents against August Brent and at -34 cents while July 7-11 went at -33 cents twice. A June 30 to July 4 CFD was also concluded at August -33 cents.

Heavy fuel was up to $1 stronger with July valued at $83.50 and August showing a 75 cent contango with September 50 cents contangoed against August. Most swaps attention was focused on July and July/August business.

Physical barges were pulled upwards and downwards with $86 heard done five times, but also $84 trading. Dealers said one party in the market wanted prices lower ahead of pricing a cargo while the other main players were pushing prices higher because of stronger bunker demand.
Low sulphur swaps were static with July pegged around $91.75 and August was put at $93. Nothing was heard concluded, but a physical cargo was heard available at $95 fob.
Gasoline stoked up a couple of dollars with July trading several times at $86.75, $87.00 and $87.25 with August backwardated by 50 cents and September effectively flat.

Naphtha swaps were slow although trade was understood to have occurred at around $180 for July, unchanged since yesterday. August and September were seen flat against July and attracting little trading attention.
